2. Recapping The Preview

This connects back to Prefix Tuning's own closing recap, already covered in Prefix Tuning. Prompt tuning was genuinely previewed there as a closely related technique with its own distinct simplification, briefly described in that earlier topic.
This topic genuinely gives it the complete, dedicated treatment already promised, exploring every detail already hinted at generally in that earlier topic.
3. Recapping Prefix Tuning
This connects back to prefix tuning, already covered in Prefix Tuning. Prefix tuning genuinely added trainable vectors at every single layer of the model.
Prompt tuning genuinely simplifies that considerably by touching only the genuinely very first input layer, the exact core simplification explored throughout the rest of this topic.

blocks.text: 4. Only One Input Level Prefix
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446294095-307756911.png
This connects back to recapping prefix tuning, already covered in this topic. Prompt tuning genuinely adds trainable vectors only at the model's own initial input embedding layer.
Every genuinely deeper layer inside the model genuinely receives no direct trainable addition at all, a genuinely minimal footprint explored throughout the rest of this topic.
5. Soft Prompts Versus Hard Prompts
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446294095-560010644.png
This connects back to only one input level prefix, already covered in this topic. Genuinely hand-written prompt text, already covered generally in Prompting, is called a hard prompt.
These genuinely trainable, learned input vectors are instead called a soft prompt, a genuinely useful naming distinction explored throughout the rest of this topic.

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: This naming distinction, already covered in this topic, directly explains why prompt tuning is sometimes described as automatically learning the optimal prompt, rather than a human manually writing one, already covered generally in Prompting.

https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446294095-166465988.png

This connects back to soft prompts versus hard prompts, already covered in this topic. Genuinely touching only one single layer genuinely means considerably fewer trainable parameters than prefix tuning.
Already covered as extremely few trainable parameters in Prefix Tuning, prompt tuning genuinely goes even further, an even more extreme level of efficiency explored throughout the rest of this topic.

9. Recognizing When Prompt Tuning Is Genuinely The Right Minimalist Choice

This connects back to even fewer trainable parameters, already covered in this topic. Prompt tuning, already covered in this topic, genuinely suits very large models with abundant capacity.

This connects back to prefix tuning's own stronger per-layer influence, already covered in Prefix Tuning. Prefix tuning, already covered, remains genuinely preferable for smaller models needing more influence.
10. Worked Example
The example below directly demonstrates a soft prompt added only at the input embedding layer, already covered in this topic, contrasted with prefix tuning's own multi-layer approach.

code.content:
import random
random.seed(0)

def random_vector(dim=4):
    return [round(random.uniform(-1, 1), 2) for _ in range(dim)]

# already covered as trainable continuous vectors in Prefix Tuning
soft_prompt_length = 2
soft_prompt = [random_vector() for _ in range(soft_prompt_length)]  # already covered as one soft prompt in this topic
print(f"Soft prompt, added only at the input layer (already covered in this topic): {soft_prompt}")

num_layers = 6  # already covered generally as model depth across this course

# already covered as only one input level prefix in this topic
prompt_tuning_touches = {"input_layer": True}
for layer in range(1, num_layers):
    prompt_tuning_touches[f"layer_{layer}"] = False

# already covered as prefix tuning touching every layer in this topic
prefix_tuning_touches = {"input_layer": True}
for layer in range(1, num_layers):
    prefix_tuning_touches[f"layer_{layer}"] = True

print(f"\nPrompt tuning touches (already covered in this topic): {sum(prompt_tuning_touches.values())} of {num_layers} layers")
print(f"Prefix tuning touches (already covered in Prefix Tuning): {sum(prefix_tuning_touches.values())} of {num_layers} layers")

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: Running this example shows prompt tuning touching only a single layer while prefix tuning touches every layer of the same model, exactly the contrast already covered in this topic.

blocks.text: 11. Key Takeaways

items: Prompt tuning trims prefix tuning down to its simplest form, touching only the input layer.
Prefix tuning adds trainable vectors at every layer; prompt tuning adds them only at the input layer.
Hand-written prompt text is called a hard prompt; these learned input vectors are a soft prompt.
Touching only one layer means even fewer trainable parameters than prefix tuning already has.
Prompt tuning's relative performance gap narrows as the base model grows larger.
On very large models, prompt tuning can approach full fine-tuning's own accuracy.
Each task gets its own small, separate soft prompt, similar to LoRA's swappable adapters.
It suits very large models with abundant capacity; prefix tuning suits smaller models needing more influence.
Next up: Instruction Tuning, shifting focus from parameter efficiency to the training data itself.
